twin_rejecting.evidence: electrical.power.json's motor_current_draw (derived: [R1a.04]*[R1.25] = 1.5A*2 = 3.0A) and motor_power_draw (derived: [R5.03]*[R1a.04]*[R1.25] = 7.2*1.5*2 = 21.6W, rev 31) apply the motor's 6V-rated stall current directly to the 7.2V pack without scaling to the pack's highest voltage, contrary to electrical standards §5 and ES-14 (the skill file's own worked example for this motor family gives ~2.1A at 8.4V, not 1.5A). The revision also leaves electrical.battery_pack's maker discharge-rate unsourced against this changed load (ES-10), which this rubric states is always the work's duty when ES-10's trigger fires. Both are the revision's own written values, not inherited given values, so the revision is not fully consistent with the design it changes and the rubric's domain standards.

electrical.power.json's motor_current_draw and motor_power_draw (rev 31) apply the motor's stall-current rating, stated at 6V by its own source row (R1a.04, 'stall current @ 6V'), directly to represent current drawn from the 7.2V-nominal pack, with no restatement or adjustment for the different condition -- a rating used at a condition other than the one it was stated for.

No quantity anywhere in the design graph (electrical.motor_drivers.json, electrical.battery_pack.json, or any other node) records a driver continuous rating, peak/current-limit rating, or battery discharge-current limit, so the 3.0A/21.6W motor budget cannot be closed against either; this is a blocking specification defect (see spec_defects), not a finding against the revision, since the needed rating is absent from the whole graph and the driver/battery parts were not chosen or changed by this revision.

No series-path element on the motor rail (driver, fuse, connector, trace) carries a declared current rating anywhere in the design graph, so the lowest rating in the path cannot be identified; blocking specification defect (see spec_defects).

electrical.power.json's motor_current_draw (3.0A, a value this revision wrote) is never compared with a sourced maximum discharge rate for the NiMH cell; electrical.battery_pack.json names the Pololu #1003 NiMH cell but records no discharge-rate quantity, and the revision -- whose change affects a load on this battery -- neither sourced one nor showed the load within the maker's published discharge curve, which ES-10 states is always the work's duty.

electrical.power.json's motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw (rev 31) use the motor's rated-voltage (6V) stall current (R1a.04 = 1.5A) directly for the 7.2V-nominal pack instead of the bound I_stall,max = V_max/R with R = V_rated/I_stall = 6V/1.5A = 4Ω (at the pack's ~8.4V charged top, ≈2.1A/motor -- matching the electrical skill file's own worked example for this exact motor family). 'Use of the rated-voltage figure at a higher supply fails' per ES-14.

electrical.motor_drivers.json carries no continuous rating, peak rating, or minimum overcurrent-trip quantity anywhere in the graph (only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage, thermal_resistance), so the three required comparisons cannot be made; blocking specification defect (see spec_defects).

electrical.power's motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw are computed only at the 7.2V nominal pack voltage (R5.03); neither the top of the window (V_max ≈ 8.4V charged) nor the sagged bottom is used anywhere for the motor branch of the budget.
The rated-voltage (6V) stall current (R1a.04 = 1.5A) is used directly for the 7.2V/higher pack-voltage budget calculation in electrical.power -- the same evidence as ES-14.

The revision's own written quantities (electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw) compute the motor's current/power only at the nominal 7.2V pack condition; redoing the check at the pack's highest voltage, as electrical standards §4/§5 require, fails (I_stall,max ≈ 2.1A/motor at ~8.4V vs. the recorded 1.5A/motor used in the written values) -- the same written values found unmet under ES-1, ES-14 and EP-4/EP-5.

electrical.power's no_change_justified asserts the motor branch current and power bounds are unchanged, but the design's own given data (supply_voltage 7.2 V, already above the motor's 6 V rated voltage) shows the true stall current is at least 1.8 A, not the 1.5 A the revision carried forward into its own written motor_current_draw (3.0 A) and motor_power_draw (21.6 W) fields. This repeats EP-5's named antipattern and ES-14's fail condition, using values the revision itself re-sourced and wrote.

electrical.motor_drivers carries no continuous current rating or peak/current-limit rating anywhere in the design graph (parts sheet rows R4.06 'peak output current' and R4.07 'peak drive current (absolute max)' are both null), so electrical.power's motor_current_draw (3.0 A, written) and motor_power_draw (21.6 W, written) cannot be shown to close against any rating.
The same missing driver current ratings (R4.06/R4.07 null, nothing recorded in electrical.motor_drivers) block determining whether the rail's credited limit is the lowest rating in its series path.

The motor load changed (#3073 to #3074) but no comparison of the pack's motor-branch current (3.0 A as recorded, and at least 1.8-2.1 A per motor once correctly scaled) against the NiMH cell's maker-sourced 4C discharge limit exists anywhere in the design graph, old or new.

electrical.power.supply_voltage (7.2 V) and electrical.motors' 6 V rating are the only voltages ever used for the motor branch; no check anywhere uses the battery window's open-circuit top or the sagged bottom, even though the revision's own written current/power values are what such a check would need to use.

electrical.motors.stall_current (1.5 A, re-sourced to the #3074 page by this revision) is used directly as the branch's stall figure in electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw even though the design's own given supply_voltage (7.2 V) already exceeds the motor's 6 V rated voltage; R = 6 V/1.5 A = 4 ohm, so at 7.2 V alone I_stall is about 1.8 A, not 1.5 A, matching the skill file's own worked example for this exact motor.

No comparison of any stall-current figure against electrical.motor_drivers' continuous rating, peak rating or minimum OCP trip exists; none of those three DRV8838 figures is recorded in the design graph or the parts sheet (R4.06-R4.08 null), and the driver itself was not chosen or changed by this revision.

The motor branch (electrical.motors, electrical.power) is checked only at the 6 V rated / 7.2 V nominal pair; no check anywhere uses the battery window's charged top or sagged bottom, confirming the 'one battery voltage' antipattern for the written current/power figures.

The #3074 motor's stall current is recorded and used at its 6 V rated voltage (1.5 A) while the pack's nominal voltage (7.2 V, given and recorded in electrical.power) is higher, confirming the antipattern exactly as the skill file names it.

The motor branch's current/power figures pass only at the rated/nominal condition (6 V/7.2 V) while the same check, applied at the battery's own given nominal 7.2 V alone (let alone its charged top), would already yield about 1.8 A rather than the recorded 1.5 A; the failing values (electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw, electrical.motors.stall_current) are ones this revision wrote (their cited source rows were changed from the #3073/R1.03 rows to the #3074/R1a.12 rows).

design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json 'torque_peak' and 'reaction_moment' (both 81.5 kgf*cm, source 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.17]') and 'no_load_speed' (0.618 rad/s, source 'derived: [R1.10] / [R2.17]'), propagated to control.balance_loop.json 'torque_peak' and control.speed_loop.json 'no_load_speed', multiply/divide the gearmotor's already-geared output-shaft rating (R1.07 = 0.74 kgf*cm, R1.10 = 650 rpm, both quoted at product 3073's output shaft) by the OVERALL gear ratio [R2.17] = 110.2, which already includes the internal ~51.45:1 reduction (confirmed by electrical.motors.json's own gear_ratio = 51.45 field, same source). This double-counts the internal reduction. knowledge/mechanical/skill.md's own worked example for this exact kit computes the wheel-axle torque as the same 0.74 kgf*cm stall figure multiplied only by the external ratio (2.88 for 49:17), giving 0.209 N*m - applying that method to this revision's own chosen ratio (0.74 x 2.14 external) gives about 1.58 kgf*cm, not the 81.5 kgf*cm written. The revision is therefore not internally consistent with the design's own sourced methodology.

design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json 'torque_peak'/'reaction_moment' = 81.5 kgf*cm and control.balance_loop.json 'torque_peak' = 81.5 kgf*cm (about 8 N*m) are implausible against the motor rating and the ratio: R1.07 (0.74 kgf*cm) is the gearmotor's own output-shaft stall torque (already past its internal ~51.45:1 reduction, per electrical.motors.json's gear_ratio=51.45 from the same product page), so multiplying it again by the OVERALL ratio [R2.17]=110.2 double-applies the internal reduction. knowledge/mechanical/skill.md's worked example for this same kit multiplies the same 0.74 kgf*cm figure only by the EXTERNAL ratio (2.88 for 49:17) to reach 0.209 N*m at the axle; applying that to this revision's chosen 2.14 external ratio gives about 1.58 kgf*cm, roughly 50x less than the 81.5 kgf*cm written. The same pattern inflates the error in no_load_speed (0.618 rad/s is about 50x too slow against the same external-ratio-only method). This value was rewritten by the revision (changed from the prior 110 kgf*cm/0.459 rad/s using R2.11), so it is a written value judged normally, not a shielded given value.

Trigger present: the revision resizes a gear ratio (mechanical.gearboxes/drivetrain gear_ratio 148.3 -> 110.2, external_gear_ratio 2.88 -> 2.14). The derived-bound sub-check (wheel torque <= usable gearmotor torque x external ratio) fails on the revision's own written torque_peak/reaction_moment figures, which use the overall ratio instead of the external ratio (same defect as MS-3), making the 'usable torque' side of this inequality wrong by about 50x. Two further sub-checks cannot be judged on written values: the traction sub-check (tractive force <= mu_s*N) needs a floor friction coefficient, which the account lists among quantities 'the parts sheet gives for no part' (a stand-in absence under clause B, so that sub-check is noted, not blocking, not a finding); and 'the work states which limit governs, and a margin with its reason' is an unwritten record (the account states this revision wrote no margin computation), also noted under clause B. Because the derived-bound sub-check fails on a written value, the item overall is unmet.

The revision is internally consistent in its arithmetic and in its MS-5 follow-ups (design/journal.jsonl revisions 30 through 38; mechanical.gearboxes.json, mechanical.drivetrain.json, control.balance_loop.json, firmware.balance_task.json, control.speed_loop.json, firmware.speed_task.json, firmware.odometry.json, firmware.main.json), but it recomputes mechanical.gearboxes.reaction_moment and torque_peak, and control.balance_loop.torque_peak, as row R1.07 times row R2.20 equals 71.2 kgf times cm, using row R1.07, labeled stall torque at 6V in parts_sheet.json, while the design own electrical.battery_pack and electrical.power nodes record a 7.2 V supply, with no stated basis for applying the 6V-rated figure at 7.2V, contrary to standards section 1 and the skill file load-case step 2, and its own worked example for this exact gearmotor and pack pairing. This is not consistent with the design it changes or with the rubric MS-6 and MS-3.

mechanical.gearboxes.reaction_moment and torque_peak, and control.balance_loop.torque_peak, all 71.2 kgf times cm, are computed from row R1.07, a stall torque the parts sheet labels stall torque at 6V, while the same design graph electrical.battery_pack and electrical.power nodes, unchanged by this revision but readable in it, record the pack supply_voltage as 7.2 V. The value is not checked against this neighbouring, directly relevant value, and no basis is stated for treating a 6V-rated stall figure as valid at 7.2V operation.

The gearbox stall-torque reaction load case (mechanical.gearboxes.reaction_moment, design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json, also control.balance_loop.torque_peak) is taken from row R1.07, stall torque at 6V in parts_sheet.json, not at the design actual 7.2 V supply voltage recorded in electrical.battery_pack and electrical.power, with no stated basis, contrary to standards section 1, which requires the drive stall-torque reaction to be taken at the voltage the design runs at, and the skill file load-case step 2, which names exactly this Balboa gearmotor and 7.2V-pack combination as needing such a stated basis.

design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json's reaction_moment/torque_peak (62.5 kgf*cm, source 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.23]') and no_load_speed (0.806 rad/s, source 'derived: [R1.10] / [R2.23]'), copied into design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json and design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json, multiply/divide the gearmotor's already-geared stall torque and no-load speed (parts_sheet.json rows R1.07=0.74 kgf*cm, R1.10=650 rpm, both from product 3073's own output-shaft spec) by the OVERALL ratio R2.23=84.4 (parts_sheet.json: 'overall gear ratio, 50:1 gearmotor with 41:25 external gearbox'), instead of by the node's own separately-recorded external_gear_ratio=1.64 (R2.06). The mechanical skill file's worked drive-sizing example (knowledge/mechanical/skill.md, 'Procedure: drive sizing and traction') uses this identical 0.74 kgf*cm figure multiplied only by the external ratio (2.88) to get the axle torque, confirming the overall ratio double-counts the gearmotor's own internal 50:1 reduction. The revision's own counts_per_wheel_revolution (1010) correctly uses the overall ratio because its base row (R3.02, pre-gearbox encoder counts) needs it -- showing the revision is internally inconsistent in how it treats the overall vs. external ratio. This is a value the revision itself wrote (changed from 110/0.459 using R2.11, to 62.5/0.806 using R2.23), so it is judged normally and is unmet.

mechanical.gearboxes.json's torque_peak/reaction_moment (62.5 kgf*cm) and no_load_speed (0.806 rad/s) are inconsistent with the node's own neighbouring external_gear_ratio field (1.64) and with the gearmotor's already-geared source rows R1.07/R1.10: using the overall ratio (gear_ratio=84.4) instead of external_gear_ratio (1.64) inflates/deflates these figures by roughly the internal 50:1 factor versus what the skill file's own worked example (knowledge/mechanical/skill.md, drive sizing procedure) computes for an analogous configuration (0.74 kgf*cm x external 2.88 = 0.209 N*m, i.e. about 2.13 kgf*cm, not ~110 kgf*cm as the unrevised value or 62.5 kgf*cm as the new one).

This is a written-value defect decidable purely by reading the record (no additional unwritten computation is needed to see the metric is unnamed), so it is a fail under the Unwritten-records carve-out ('a check that involves a written value, that the values on the page decide by reading, and that fails, is judged normally'). Skill 'estimating driver junction temperature' step 4 and standards.md §6 both require the metric to be named because RθJA and RθJB are not interchangeable in TJ = T_reference x P: RθJA pairs with ambient temperature, RθJB pairs with a measured board temperature, and conflating them would understate a real TJ estimate.
